mechanism_narrative: A sustained low federal funds rate (below 2.0%) compresses discount rates and boosts equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 2.0%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in unemployment exceeding 0.2 percentage points over three months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered instances, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous rises in federal funds rate and inflation (FEDFUNDS > 0.1pp and CPIAUCSL > 0.2pp in 3 months) signal aggressive monetary tightening, reducing equity valuations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises > 0.1pp and CPIAUCSL rises > 0.2pp in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered instances, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL YoY change > 5%), the Federal Reserve's aggressive tightening reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL YoY change exceeds 5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

candidate_trigger: PAYEMS falls > 0.5% and UNRATE rises > 0.1pp in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered instances, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
